QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_34

question.text: The SIA is assessing a women-empowerment programme where the SE reports 'Increased bargaining power within household'. Under SAS-400, this qualitative indicator is BEST captured through:

answer.text: Mixed-method: paired Likert-scale items (pre-post), vignette-based decision-making questions, and sub-sample FGD; husbands interviewed separately to check consistency

explanation.text: The Logic: Mixed-method with husband cross-interview reduces social-desirability bias. FGD adds context. Paired Likert pre-post gives quantitative movement. This layered approach is audit-defensible under SAS-400. The Trap: Option A is single-source self-report bias. Option C is SE internal. Option D is tangential. Cross-Exam Context: Mixed-method psychometric approach overlaps XV (Research Analyst — investor-survey design) and V-B (MF Foundation). Assessor's Pro-Tip: For household-bargaining indicators, ALWAYS include husband sub-interviews. The delta between wife-reported and husband-reported bargaining power is itself a useful finding.
